title: Doppler Effect
body:
The **Doppler effect** shifts the wavelength of light from a source moving along the line of
sight. Receding sources shift toward longer wavelengths, which is redshift, and approaching
sources shift toward shorter ones, which is blueshift.

$$
\frac{\Delta\lambda}{\lambda_0} = \frac{v}{c}
$$

The measurement is precise because the rest wavelengths are known from laboratory
[[Spectra|spectra]], so the shift of a recognisable line pattern gives the speed directly. It
detects only motion toward or away from the observer, and motion across the sky produces no
shift at all.

Four results in the course come from it:

```
binary star masses      the two spectra shift in opposite directions as they orbit
exoplanets              a star wobbles as an unseen planet pulls on it
galactic rotation       one edge of a galaxy approaches while the other recedes
cosmic expansion        distant galaxies are redshifted, which gives Hubble's Law
```

The cosmological redshift is worth separating from the others. It comes from space expanding
while the light is in transit, with the galaxy at rest in the space around it, and the two
mechanisms produce the same observation.
